questions.topic: An eastern bloc treaty presented as mutual defence
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks how the treaty integrated militaries; explain.

answer.exemplar: The treaty integrated militaries by placing forces under a unified command structure controlled by the leading state, standardizing equipment and doctrine.

questions.explanation: Integration placed forces under unified command. The tempting equality or independence claims misstate the arrangement.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: Britain's exit from Greece and the containment policy

stimulus.body: A diplomat warns that if one region falls, neighbors will follow. He urges aid to stabilize vulnerable governments before pressure becomes collapse.

questions.stem: A clinician's note reviews a containment source; what logic does it express?

options.text: Regions should be left to collapse
No aid is needed for stability
Regional stability requires supporting vulnerable governments

questions.explanation: The source argues stability needs support for vulnerable governments. The tempting collapse or military-only claims contradict the text.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: An Asian state enters the western alliance
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks for a synthesis of alliance entry effects; which summary is best?

options.text: Entry had no regional or strategic effects
Entry aligned the state with the west and reshaped regional power
Entry isolated the state from all allies

questions.explanation: Entry aligned the state with the west and reshaped regional power. The tempting no-effect or isolation claims misstate the outcome.
